model_description: RADIX ABLATION (not a submission). Same architecture and algorithm as the base-10 scratchpad, but the interleaved-Horner loop runs in BASE 2 (one bit per step, NB=16 for p<2^16) instead of base 10 (one decimal digit per step). Purpose: quantify steps-vs-drift — base-2 spends ~3x the steps of base-10 at the same tier, so if the long-scratchpad ceiling is a rollout-drift problem (as recurrent_v6 and Sneiderman's base-2 neural-horner both indicate), base-2 tier-3 should trail base-10 tier-3. Per step: m=a*bit, t=acc*2+m, acc=t mod p; R=acc, returned as decimal digits. WIDTH=16 bits covers tiers 1-3.
training_description: Trained from scratch (base-2 vocab differs from base-10, so no warm-start) on tiers 1-3 with a held-out prime split and an operand-magnitude curriculum, d384/8L/~11M. Compared against the base-10 recurrent_v3/v5 tier-3 numbers in one harness to isolate the radix (step-count) effect. Compliant: worked steps are training targets, answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation), a%p/b%p legal reductions, no hand-coded arithmetic. See dev/train_recurrent.py.
